items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: And I played with Silly Stamp Band, made up a band, not our, he made the band up. This was in around, last of 41.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, all those numbers, yeah. I never heard anybody do that until about 1945, when once Jim Robinson and George Lewis. Oh yeah, that's... They played it way back though.

Yeah, they did, yeah, they played that way back. Really, he was a real great musician. And I played with Silly Stamp Band, made up a band, not our, he made the band up. This was in around, last of 41. He had, things had gotten bad and he had broke up his band. He didn't have any band, Silly Stamp, Papa Silly Stamp.
Yeah, I remember, while he was out.

items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1961-02-24
items.q: Oh yeah, Celestan. I worked with him in 41 he made up a band.

ctx.x: Did you ever work with Papa Celestan?

Oh yeah, Celestan. I worked with him in 41 he made up a band. And at that time he had quit playing for a while, almost like give it up. And he started to make up a band. So I was playing with him and for then when the war come up you had to get a defense job. And he got a job now at the shipyard at Higgins. And some guy got loose with a car and run over to a gang of people and he was one of the guys that got hit. And we had played together, had a band of about two or three months, and after he got hit and…
Who did he have in those times when you were with him?
